15-minute Mediterranean warm green lentils

Tender cooked brown lentils warmed with shallots, cumin, lemon zest, baby spinach, and crumbled creamy goat cheese.

Prep
5 min prep
Total / resting
15 min total
Ingredients & Method ↓

Development edition · Awaits kitchen testing.

Ingredients Method Storage

Ingredients

How many people?
2

Estimated to serve 2 people as a comforting meal.

  • 1 can cooked brown or green lentils, rinsed and drained
    Package size: 15 oz / 400 g.
  • 1 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 medium shallot, finely chopped
  • 1 garlic clove, minced
  • ½ tsp ground cumin
  • ¼ tsp ground coriander
  • 2 cups (60.0 g) baby spinach leaves
  • 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, plus ½ tsp grated lemon zest
  • ⅓ cup (50.0 g) crumbled goat cheese or feta
  • Salt and black pepper, to taste
  • 2 tbsp water or vegetable broth

Contains milk (goat cheese / feta).

Method

01

Soften the aromatics.

Heat olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook for 4-5 minutes until softened. Add garlic and cumin, cooking for another minute until fragrant.

02

Warm the lentils.

Add the drained lentils and 2 tablespoons of water or broth. Simmer gently for 4–5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until hot throughout.

03

Wilt greens and brighten.

Stir in the spinach leaves in batches until just wilted (about 1 minute). Remove pan from heat and stir in lemon juice, lemon zest, salt, and pepper.

Look for: Lentils are warmed through and tender, but not mushy.

04

Plate and top.

Transfer to warm bowls. Scatter crumbled goat cheese or feta over top and finish with a light drizzle of olive oil.

Why it works: Cumin and coriander bloom quickly in warm oil, coating the lentils with earthy fragrance. Lemon juice and zest added off the heat keeps the citrus bright against the warm spices.

Serve with

Delicious served as a standalone warm lunch with sourdough toast, or spooned over roasted sweet potatoes for dinner.

One way to change it up

Swap canned brown lentils with cooked French Puy lentils. Dairy-free? Replace goat cheese with toasted walnuts or pumpkin seeds for richness and crunch.

A small technique note

Rinse canned lentils thoroughly under cold water to remove excess sodium and canning brine, then drain well before simmering with olive oil and spices.

Storage & Prep ahead

This recipe awaits kitchen testing. A refrigerated shelf life has not yet been established.
